security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI M-mode SBI handler for sbi_covh_connect_device() or sbi_covh_get_device_connection_transcript() writes SPDM connection transcript data to an S-mode-supplied buffer pointer (connection_data_addr_out / data_addr_out) without first validating that the entire [addr, addr+size) range lies within the calling domain's accessible memory as defined by PMP/ePMP entries, or without verifying the 4KB alignment requirement, or without sanitizing the transcript_element_id enum to its 4 valid values (0-3) before indexing into internal transcript data structures
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: SBI handler receives guest-physical buffer pointer + size via a6/a7 (or equivalent) from S-mode, writes M-mode-managed secret material (SPDM session transcript, certificate chains, device measurements) to that buffer based solely on caller-supplied bounds, without first walking the domain's PMP/ePMP configuration to confirm the buffer does not straddle into M-mode-only or peer-domain memory
security_spec.summary: New CoVE-IO SBI calls pass SPDM transcript/certificate data from M-mode to S-mode via caller-supplied shared memory buffers; missing PMP-based buffer validation allows a malicious S-mode domain manager to exfiltrate M-mode-managed SPDM secrets into arbitrary physical memory regions or probe M-mode memory layout

findings.finding: No firmware implementation exists to audit. The PR defines SPDM data structures and CoVE-IO API flows in specification documents only (09-coveio_abi.adoc, 07-theory_operations.adoc). The vulnerability pattern — SBI handlers writing SPDM transcript data to S-mode-supplied buffer pointers without PMP/ePMP validation, alignment checks, or transcript_element_id sanitization — would apply to any future implementation. This is a forward-looking risk: when these handlers are implemented in C, they must validate that [addr, addr+size) lies within the calling domain's PMP/ePMP-accessible memory, enforce 4KB alignment, and bounds-check transcript_element_id to {0,1,2,3} before indexing.
